OPERATION NOTE

Patient's Name: [redacted]
Date of birth: [redacted]
Gender: female
Hospital number: [redacted]
NHS number: [redacted]

Date of Surgery: [redacted]

Post-op Diagnosis: Displaced intracapsular fracture neck of femur, right

Procedure(s): Right Hip Hemiarthroplasty; Cerclage wiring of intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture - Right

Patient Class: Inpatient (trauma list)

Consultant on Case: [redacted]

Surgeons:
* [redacted] - Consultant
* [redacted] - Primary Operator (Registrar)
* [redacted] - Assisting

Anaesthetist: [redacted]
Responsible Anaesthetist: [redacted]
Anaesthetic Type: spinal, peripheral nerve block
ASA Grade: III

Indication: 82 year old admitted after a fall at home with a displaced intracapsular fracture of the right neck of femur, confirmed on plain film and CT. Booked on the trauma list for hemiarthroplasty.

Description of Procedure

WHO checklist completed. IV teicoplanin and gentamicin given at induction. Lateral position with front and back bolsters. Skin prepped with betadine and chlorhexidine, iodine-impregnated incise drape.

Anterolateral approach to proximal right femur. Dissection through fat and fascia lata. Gluteus medius and minimus incised from the greater trochanter. T-shaped capsulotomy. Femoral neck cut 1cm above the lesser trochanter. Femoral head removed, measured 44mm.

Femur prepared with box chisel, pencil reamers and raspers sequential to size 2. During broaching of the femoral canal a longitudinal crack was noted extending from the calcar down the medial cortex of the proximal femoral shaft, approximately 4cm in length, with no displacement. This was considered an intraoperative periprosthetic fracture. Two cerclage wires (18-gauge) were passed around the proximal femur proximal and distal to the crack and tensioned to secure the fracture prior to proceeding with stem insertion. No further propagation was seen on trialling.

Canal prepared with pulsed lavage (1L) and dried with ribbon gauze and suction catheter. Canal cemented. Cemented stem with centraliser inserted, taking care to avoid further distraction of the cerclage-wired fracture. Trialled with standard +4mm head; equal leg lengths and a stable hip on internal and external rotation. 44mm bipolar head +4 inserted. Stable hip reduction confirmed, equal leg lengths, stable on internal and external rotation. Image intensifier check confirmed satisfactory wire position and no further fracture propagation. Saline wash.

Estimated blood loss 450ml, no transfusion required intraoperatively.

Closure
Capsule - 5 Ethibond
Gluteus medius and minimus - 5 Ethibond inter-osseous followed by continuous suture in tendon
Fascia lata - 1 Vicryl
Fat - 1 Vicryl interrupted
Subdermal - 2-0 Vicryl
Skin - 3-0 Monocryl, skin glue, steristrips

Total operative time 105 minutes.

Post op Plan
Toe-touch weight bearing on the right for 6 weeks given the periprosthetic fracture and cerclage wiring, then progress as tolerated with physiotherapy input.
Repeat plain film in recovery to confirm implant and wire position.
FBC, U+E tomorrow.
No further antibiotics needed beyond the two post-op doses.
VTE prophylaxis as per protocol for NOF fractures.
Orthopaedic follow up at 2 and 6 weeks with weight-bearing progression reviewed at 6 week appointment.

Implant(s):
Implant Name | Type | Manufacturer | Site | No. Used | Action
PALACOS R+G 2x40g bone cement | Cement / Putty | Movianto UK Ltd | Right Hip | 1 | Implanted
Stryker Orthopaedics Exeter V40 Cemented Hip Stem, size 2 | Orthopaedic Prosthesis | Stryker UK Ltd | Right Hip | 1 | Implanted
Stryker Orthopaedics UHR Universal Head Bipolar Component, OD 44mm | Orthopaedic Prosthesis | Stryker UK Ltd | Right Hip | 1 | Implanted
Stryker Orthopaedics V40 Femoral Head, OD 28mm, OFFST +4 | Orthopaedic Prosthesis | Stryker UK Ltd | Right Hip | 1 | Implanted
18-gauge cerclage wire | Fixation wire | DePuy Synthes | Right femur | 2 | Implanted

procedures.procedure_desc: Cerclage wiring of intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture, right

output.findings: During broaching of the femoral canal a longitudinal crack was noted extending from the calcar down the medial cortex of the proximal femoral shaft, approximately 4cm in length, with no displacement. Image intensifier check after cerclage wiring and stem insertion confirmed satisfactory wire position and no further fracture propagation.

complications.complication_desc: Longitudinal crack noted extending from the calcar down the medial cortex of the proximal femoral shaft, approximately 4cm in length, with no displacement, during broaching of the femoral canal - an intraoperative periprosthetic fracture.
complications.management: Two 18-gauge cerclage wires passed around the proximal femur proximal and distal to the crack and tensioned to secure the fracture prior to stem insertion; no further propagation seen on trialling or on image intensifier check.

output.operation_summary: Right hip hemiarthroplasty for a displaced intracapsular neck of femur fracture, complicated intraoperatively by a periprosthetic crack of the proximal femoral shaft during canal broaching. This was secured with two cerclage wires before proceeding with cemented stem and bipolar head insertion, with no further fracture propagation on trialling or image intensifier check. Toe-touch weight bearing advised for 6 weeks given the fracture and wiring.
